fieldValues.title: `srs://` stays tooling
fieldValues.decision_rationale: The main form of a cross-repository link is a relation (owner), so the stored form is Address components. The resource paths change often (ADR-037 carries 18 amendments since July 2026, several adding resource paths: `type/`, `tree`, `agent-index`, `context/`). A string rule can be added later at little cost; removing one breaks emitters.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The spec defines no string form for an Address; `srs://` remains srs-rust tooling (ADR-037 §6); srs#218 stays parked.
fieldValues.decision_scope: Whether the specification defines a string form for an Address: it does not; srs:// stays implementation tooling.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Specify the repository segment of srs:// strings (Revision 3). Specify a full canonical serialization (locks a path list amended 18 times since July 2026).
fieldValues.accepted_costs: No standard string to paste into prose; agents may still guess malformed strings (finding bbe9faf9, `srs://default/…`), which [R8] answers with `not-in-boundary`.
evidence_refs: srs-programme conversation container ec40e5ab (the owner's words, 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-02)
fieldValues.review_trigger:
1. A repository is published and its elements need public URLs. *Checked at:* the first published repository.
2. Links start being stored as strings inside field content across repositories. *Checked at:* the cross-repository relations RFC, which must say why a relation does not cover such a link.
3. Two implementations need to exchange `srs://` strings and disagree on them. *Checked at:* the first second implementation of the MCP surface (srs-web's browser MCP shares srs-mcp-core today, so it does not count).
